newsitem.title: IRAN: Ousted Afghan president, factions in Iran for talks.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Afghan president, factions in Iran for talks.

text.p: Ousted Afghan president Burhanuddin Rabbani and other faction leaders have arrived in Tehran for peace talks due to start on Saturday, the Iranian news agency IRNA said on Friday.
Iran has offered to host the talks to secure peace between the warring parties in Afghanistan, where the Taleban Islamic militia has made major military gains in the past week.

Ousted prime minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar and former president Sibghatullah Mojadedi were also in Tehran for the talks to which the Taleban, who seized Kabul in September, have also been invited, IRNA said.
It said Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati welcomed Rabbani on his arrival on Thursday night.
Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Alaeddin Boroujerdi, quoted by IRNA, said on Thursday no response had been received from the Taleban to the invitation.
Boroujerdi said the Taleban's response would "test their claims to peace", IRNA reported.
However, a Taleban spokesman in Afghanistan said the militia had not received any formal invitation to the talks.

"Even if we get an invitation, we will not participate in this conference because Iran is not neutral, it favours one side," Mullah Abdul Jalil, the Taleban's acting deputy foreign minister, told a Pakistan-based news service on Friday.

A Taleban spokesman said earlier this week a delegation led by acting foreign minister Mullah Mohammed Ghous was on its way to Tehran, but Taleban sources said later that the visit had been postponed until after the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan.
A senior Iranian cleric on Friday accused the Taleban of "ruthlessness" for waging war on its foes north of Kabul during Ramadan.

"A group (Taleban), which is utterly ignorant about everything, have in the name of Islam ruthlessly attacked people, taking them hostage, running them from their homes and causing destruction," Ayatollah Ahmad Jannati said in a mass Friday prayer sermon broadcast on Tehran radio.

"Are you really perfect Moslems? Then do not kill people during Ramadan...As respect for the month of Ramadan let people stay home to fast and pray. Go and pray instead of killing in the battlefield," added Jannati.

Iran, which recognises Rabbani's government, has often criticised the Taleban for giving Islam a bad name. Iranian media have blasted the Taleban as being set up by Pakistan and backed by the United States. Pakistan denies the charge.
Tehran has repeatedly called on Afghan factions to stop fighting and reach a power-sharing agreement.
